transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-28 14:21 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Navarro (Redwood SE); Alex Rowe (Sentinel - Head of ML); Priya Shah (Platform Eng); Tom Baird (FinOps); Samira Iqbal (Security); external consultant

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect)
Maya: quick walkthrough of per-route dashboards and how cost ties to tokens, batching and KV cache. Diego: shows demo of Console, drilling into a noisy route and sticky prefixes. Questions on residency, SSO and audit logs.

[00:00] Maya: All right folks, thanks for jumping on. I know we have about forty five minutes, so we'll do a focused deck + live Console demo and then leave time for questions. Myself is Maya, and Diego is our SE — he will do most of the click-throughs.
[00:12] Alex: Sounds good. For context Tom is very interested in cost attribution, Samira will poke at the security bits.
[00:20] Maya: Perfect. Diego, take it away?
[00:24] Diego: Yep. I'm going to share my screen — can everyone see the Redwood Console? It's the per-route dashboard home. Top line we show request volume, token consumption, cost per route. The view on the right is a sampled list of recent requests.
[01:02] Priya: Quick Q — how do you map our app endpoints to the Redwood routes? We have composite calls that fan out.
[01:10] Diego: Good question. You can map at the ingestion layer — route tags accept a route_id in the header or JSON payload. For composite fanouts we let you create synthetic routes and attribute using a parent_id. The attribution table will show parent/child aggregation.
[01:45] Tom: And the per-route cost — is that direct token billing or an allocation? If one composite call hits 4 models, how is that split?
[01:55] Diego: By default we show token-level raw cost per request and then we provide an allocation profile you can customize. For multi-model calls we show line-items: model A cost, model B cost, and the dashboard can show either raw or prorated allocation by latency or token share.
[02:30] Alex: Is that exportable? Tom: we want to feed into our internal FinOps.
[02:36] Maya: Yep, CSV/Parquet exports available. We can include the model, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, kernel/quantization tag, and approximate GPU seconds. Diego will send a sample export.
[02:55] Samira: On security — does the export leak PII? We need redaction and logs that show just meta.
[03:02] Diego: Exports are metadata-only by default. You can toggle to include masked prompts for troubleshooting; we also support on-prem/private deployments where ingest never leaves VPC.
[03:20] Priya: Show us the per-route cost waterfall.
[03:23] Diego: Sure — drilling into /api/chat/send we're looking at a median latency of 220ms, 95th at 480ms, token rate about 180k tokens/day, cost attribution shows batch overhead and model unit price. There's a cost waterfall: model cost, batching inefficiency, kv misses, and infra overhead.
[04:05] Diego: See this spike around 03/18 — that's when you had a long context prompt and we recompiled to a bigger kernel. The Console flags kernel switches.
[04:25] Alex: The kv cache — can we see hit rate per route?
[04:28] Diego: Yes, the cache panel shows hit/miss by route and prefix. We also show suggested prefix lengths and a projection of savings if you enable prefix caching or prefix clustering.
[04:42] Tom: Do you have a back-of-the-envelope for savings?
[04:46] Diego: For chat-ish flows we've seen 20–45% token-level cost reduction when prefix caching is tuned. For Q&A routes with repetitive prompts you can get higher. We also show estimated GPU seconds saved in the dashboard.
[05:10] Priya: About Dedicated pools — if we reserve a dedicated pool, how do you show per-route SLOs and throttling?
[05:18] Maya: You can pin routes to a pool, set admission policies and burst allowance. Console will surface queue times, throttled requests, and fallback routing to hosted variants if the pool is saturated.
[05:33] Priya: And the pricing math for dedicated — we want to compare reserved commit vs host-on-demand (burst).
[05:38] Maya: Diego has a neat demo of a commit vs pay-as-you-go calc. Diego?
[05:42] Diego: So here's the optimizer panel. Input your baseline QPS, average tokens per request, latency SLO. The model recommends a pool size and shows per-token equivalent cost for commit vs hosted. This includes utilization assumptions. The recommendation engine will also show breakeven point at N months.
[06:20] Tom: What utilization numbers do you assume? Our team sees big diurnal variance.
[06:24] Diego: The default uses 60% steady utilization with spike multiplier configurable. For diurnal we recommend autoscale windowing and a small burst buffer. We can tune the projection if you share hourly traffic.
[06:45] Alex: How do we handle multi-region? We have EU data residency needs.
[06:50] Maya: Redwood supports region-aware routing. You can tag routes by region and we show per-region cost and capacity. For Private or on-prem we can run control plane in your region or hybrid.
[07:10] Samira: SSO and audit logs — we need SAML SSO and per-token audit trails for compliance.
[07:16] Diego: We support SAML/SCIM SSO and RBAC. Audit logs include route-level events—deploys, rollouts, config changes, and exportable request-level metadata. We also have KMS integrations and can provide an audit trail sample.
[07:38] Priya: Show a sample of the request-level drilldown.
[07:41] Diego: Clicking a single request — you can see timestamps, token counts, model variant used, kernel, batch_id, and whether cache hit occurred. Text is redacted by default.
[08:10] Alex: Can we do retention controls? Our regulatory team requires 30 day raw retention and longer meta retention.
[08:16] Maya: Yes, retention settings are per-environment. Hosted defaults to 30 days raw and 365 days metadata, but on Private you can control entirely.
[08:28] Priya: On the route naming — we have ephemeral dev routes. Is there tagging and filtering?
[08:33] Diego: Yup tags, labels, and regex-based filters. You can set automated TTL for ephemeral routes so they age out.
[08:47] Tom: Drill into the cost breakdown for that high-frequency route you flagged.
[08:51] Diego: This route shows 42% of tokens but only 18% of revenue because the model used is cheaper. The bigger cost driver is kv misses and small-batch overhead. If you increase batch windows from 10ms to 40ms you see a 12% cost drop in this simulation.
[09:20] Alex: What about model quantization flags — can we see which requests used quantized kernels?
[09:25] Diego: Yes kernel tags are surfaced per request. You can filter by quantized runs vs fp16. The optimizer suggests quantization when quality thresholds are maintained.
[09:40] Samira: Any point about PII in logs again — where does redact happen? At ingestion or at export?
[09:45] Diego: We redact at ingestion in hosted default. In Private you can choose to ingest raw locally and redact downstream. Our recommendation is redact upstream unless you need raw.
[09:58] Alex: On the billing side — can we map to our internal cost centers? We have teams mapped by tag.
[10:03] Diego: You can attach cost tags to routes; exports include cost_center and team tags. We also support a cost allocation matrix upload.
[10:20] Priya: Can you demo a custom dashboard we might want — e.g., per-feature view where features touch multiple routes?
[10:26] Diego: Sure — I'm creating a custom dashboard now: add widget -> grouped by tag feature:recommendation, show token trend and cost per 1k requests. You can save and share links with specific RBAC visibility.
[11:05] Maya: Quick interjection — on typical POCs we ask for 4–6 routes that represent your critical spend; we instrument them and run a 2 week pilot to surface wins.
[11:16] Alex: That's fine. We'll pick chat send, vector-encode, moderation, and rerank.
[11:22] Tom: Can you show an example of an action we might take from the Console? Like turning on prefix caching?
[11:28] Diego: Yep — in the route detail there's a recommendations tab: "Enable prefix_cache with prefix_len=40, batch_window=25ms". You can apply from the UI or export as terraform.
[11:45] Priya: Terraform support — nice. Is that config under our control or does Redwood manage the rollout?
[11:50] Maya: You can choose manual or managed rollouts. Managed rollouts will canary across a percentage of traffic and monitor regression in quality.
[12:06] Samira: About regressions — how do we measure quality? BLEU style? We need `no regression` guarantees for high priority flows.
[12:14] Diego: We integrate evals and prompt-sets. You can pin golden prompts and measure metrics like exact match, ROUGE, and custom heuristics. If a canary deviates beyond thresholds we'll auto rollback.
[12:32] Alex: Any live examples of a rollback?
[12:35] Diego: In the rollout history you can see previous deploys and the auto-rollback flag tripped when latency increased 2x during a kernel change.
[12:48] Tom: A question on unit economics — what do you include in per-token cost? GPU time only? Or infra and support fees?
[12:55] Maya: The default per-token in the dashboard includes model inference cost + infra overhead + a small platform fee. For dedicated we surface amortized committed costs and delta to hosted. We can produce a full TCO export.
[13:16] Priya: We use long prompts that include KB context; how do you show chunking cost?
[13:22] Diego: The transcript viewer will show the chunking flow: number of context chunks retrieved, embeddings calls, and rerank steps. Each step is broken down in the waterfall.
[13:38] Alex: Let's talk about custom sampling — can we instrument a subset of traffic to trace end-to-end?
[13:44] Diego: Yes sample rates are configurable and you can attach debugging payloads. Those sampled requests are preserved longer and include masked text for root cause.
[13:55] Tom: Any limits on export size? We want daily dumps into S3.
[13:59] Maya: No hard limits for enterprise customers — we support scheduled S3 exports and incremental deltas.
[14:12] Priya: Back to the optimizer panel — can it recommend quantization per route?
[14:16] Diego: It can. It will recommend quantization profile and show a projected quality delta. You can run a canary to validate.
[14:30] Alex: Competitors question — our infra team asked if Redwood integrates with our existing model registry and CI.
[14:36] Diego: We have webhooks and a model registry connector; we can pull model artifacts and register model versions. CI/CD triggers can drive rollouts.
[14:52] Samira: On encryption — KMS integration specifics? We use an HSM customer key for some PII.
[14:58] Maya: We support BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations; for Private you can also control keys on-prem. We can share architecture docs.
[15:10] Priya: Could you toggle on the cost-per-route trend and annotate a recent anomaly?
[15:14] Diego: Here — on 03/10 you see an anomaly correlated to an upstream spike and a model variant change. The dashboard annotates deploys and kernel switch events.
[15:34] Alex: About the per-token price — can we model a scenario where we move rerank to a smaller model?
[15:38] Diego: Sure — the optimizer lets you simulate model swaps and shows delta on latency and cost; you can compare 7B quantized vs 13B fp16.
[15:55] Tom: If we want to run a pilot on Dedicated — how long to stand up a pool?
[15:59] Maya: Typically 24–72 hours for capacity, depending on region and hardware. We can pre-warm via burst credits for initial ramp.
[16:11] Priya: How do we measure success of the pilot? What metrics do you track?
[16:16] Diego: We track cost delta, latency SLO adherence, error rate, cache hit rate, and quality regressions on pinned prompts. We'll share a pilot success template.
[16:32] Alex: Any case study for similar customers?
[16:35] Maya: We have a mid-market SaaS that reduced per-token cost by 33% with route-level caching and dedicated commit. I'll send that writeup.
[16:46] Priya: Questions about billing frequency — can we do monthly or annual?
[16:50] Maya: Both. Dedicated reserved is typically annual/quarterly commits; hosted is monthly.
[16:58] Tom: Can Redwood surface anomaly alerts into our PagerDuty?
[17:03] Diego: Yes events can forward to PagerDuty, Slack, or webhooks with threshold triggers.
[17:15] Alex: A couple of small feature asks from my team — show cost per feature (not per route) and allow tagging by release.
[17:24] Maya: Feature request noted. We can map route tags to feature and show aggregated cost per feature. Diego: we actually have that in beta.
[17:36] Samira: Before we wrap — we need sample SOC2 artifacts and export of audit logs to evaluate.
[17:41] Maya: Will attach SOC2 attestation and a sample audit export.
[17:48] Alex: Great. On next steps we'll share 6 routes and Redwood will send cost CSV and schedule pilot kickoff.
[17:55] Diego: I'll mark the route IDs we demoed and include recommendations in the export.
[18:02] Priya: Anything about fallback behavior — if dedicated fails does traffic go to hosted and is there double billing?
[18:08] Diego: Fallback is policy-driven. You can allow automatic fallback to hosted variants; billing is charged on the serving resource used, so you pay for hosted usage during fallback. No double billing for the same request.
[18:28] Alex: One last thing — can we get per-route token histograms?
[18:31] Diego: Yes histograms and percentile breakdowns are available.
[18:36] Maya: Okay I think that's a good place to stop. We'll follow up with the export and a proposed pilot schedule. Thanks everyone.
[18:45] Tom: Thanks all.
[18:47] Samira: Thanks.
[18:50] Alex: Appreciate it.
